# Results ledger (auto-generated — do not edit by hand)

Generated by `scripts/make_results_ledger.py` from the committed `results/*.csv`; regenerate after the pipeline. Every result value here is read from an output file or computed from one in this generator, so it cannot go stale against the code (approximate narrative scales carry a ~). All absolute numbers are PRELIMINARY where noted — they ride on the OPEN beam waist $w_0$ (README §2.5). Frequencies are transition-axis unless a `_LASER` note says otherwise.

> **The dominant systematic is the OPEN beam waist $w_0$ — a direct beam-profile measurement (knife-edge and/or camera) in a fixed-lock session would measure it; that session is proposed, not scheduled.** The M9 transit Monte-Carlo flux bug (it ran ~2× too narrow) was FIXED and fully propagated on 2026-07-13: the corrected transit disfavours the old 32 µm nominal — in the thin single-waist limit, natural convolved with transit alone already exceeds the observed ~5.25 MHz line there, though over a realistic multi-mm collection column that margin narrows and the line alone no longer decides it; the independent 64 µm waist measurement (Nieddu/Rajasree) is what makes the exclusion safe. Since v3.0.0 that measurement IS the prior: $w_0$ is **64 µm** (band 60–70), adopted from the lineage rather than inferred from our own line, and the retro ratio is $\rho=0.94\pm0.04$ rather than an asserted 1. Every $w_0$-conditional number below (the $\beta_\text{self}$ and $\sigma_\text{laser}$ bounds, $S_0$, the $w_0$-band) has been RE-RUN at the adopted prior; they stay PRELIMINARY and $w_0$-conditional because the transit vs $\sigma_\text{laser}$ degeneracy means the archival line cannot pin $w_0$ itself — that is the beam-profile measurement's job. An earlier note inferred $w_0\approx90$ µm from a second (spurious) factor-of-2; retracted — see `docs/notes/transit_width_resolved.md`, `literature_food_for_thought.md`.

## C1 — collisional self-broadening $\beta_\text{self}$

Three estimators of the SAME quantity under DIFFERENT $\sigma_\text{laser}$
treatments. They span a **factor $\sim$2** (0.03–0.05) — that
model-dependence IS the C1 uncertainty, larger than any single fit's error
bar, and it is the headline uncertainty. The **conservative model-independent
bound (per-peak 95% range 0.21–0.43; floored at the
loosest, $<0.43$) is the robust floor**; the fits are PRELIMINARY
cross-checks pending a fixed-lock session.

| estimator | value (MHz per $10^{12}$ cm$^{-3}$) | status |
|---|---|---|
| model-independent width-slope (95% bound, per peak: $t(1)=6.31\times$syst, then $\times1.2$ density-scale) | 993.4121 nm $<$ 0.32; 993.4154 nm $<$ 0.43; 993.4192 nm $<$ 0.21; 993.4207 nm $<$ 0.42 | **headline BOUND** (geometry-robust) |

> Bound construction (corrected 2026-07-16 — two coverage fixes). (i) **Student-t, not 2σ:** the between-block scatter that dominates the slope error is estimated on only **1 residual DOF** (3 density points, 2 fit params), so a one-sided 95% needs $t(0.95, 1) = 6.31$, not the Gaussian-asymptotic 2 used before — the old “$\approx$2σ” bounds (0.07–0.15) under-covered, which is why they were always flagged with a ~factor-2 own-uncertainty; the t-quantile formalizes exactly that. (ii) **Density scale:** $\beta \propto 1/N$, so the ~20% spread between published vapor-pressure correlations moves every $\beta$ by 20%; the cold-spot direction makes the fitted $\beta$ an UNDERestimate, so the bound is inflated on the + side ($\times$1.2; `density.py`). **The per-peak spread is systematics, not physics:** the bounds track each peak's `resid_rms` (0.23/0.34/0.15/0.29), not a physical rate — all four have SNR $<$ 2 (none resolves collisions). Because the min of noisy 1-DOF estimates is the down-fluctuated one, the **loosest** peak is the single-number floor to quote; taking the tightest would be selection bias. Quote the range, floor at the loosest. (iii) **What the 95% conditions on:** the t-quantile covers *exchangeable* between-block scatter; a *monotone* session drift aliased onto the monotone T-vs-time acquisition would bias the slope with a sign no scatter quantile covers, and the per-peak `monotonic` flags (2/4 peaks non-monotonic) cannot discriminate that confound — it is held by the BOUND framing itself, not by the quantile (`beta.collisional_slope` docstring). The 130 °C lever variant (dof = 2, in the CSV) is far tighter but carries its own caveat — **not** that it is a different session. The recovered clock places it 2.3 h before the 110 °C dwell, inside the same continuous campaign, while the 9.6 h break falls *between* 110 °C and 90 °C. What it is: a 4.5 h power-ladder block at the extreme end of the density lever, and folding an extreme lever point in moves the answer by leverage rather than by physics.

| per-peak fits ($\sigma_\text{laser}$ free per peak) | 993.4121 nm 0.026(8); 993.4154 nm 0.026(8); 993.4192 nm 0.030(4); 993.4207 nm 0.045(6) | PRELIM (993.4207 nm ~1.6σ above 993.4121 nm) |
| hierarchical ($\sigma_\text{laser}$ shared per-T across peaks; $\beta$ per isotope) | 85Rb 0.053(4); 87Rb 0.053(5) | PRELIM — the (·) is **STAT-only**; the dominant systematic (the unverifiable per-T timing assumption, below) is unquantified, so this is not a %-precise measurement |

> Why the hierarchical $\beta$ can exceed BOTH per-peak values (not a contradiction): it is not a pooling of them. Sharing one $\sigma_\text{laser}(T)$ across the four peaks pins the laser width lower at high density (110 °C), so more width is assigned to collisions than when each peak floats its own $\sigma_\text{laser}$. But that per-T sharing **assumes the four peaks at a given T saw the same laser width**. Its usual justification — that they were acquired close in time — is now MEASURABLY FALSE: the recovered clock (`data_recovered/CLOCK.csv`) dates the four peak-blocks of each dwell **54–76 minutes apart** (70 °C: 76 min; 90 °C: 54 min; 110 °C: 65 min), not minutes apart. What the clock also shows is that the widths do not track that elapsed time — pooled dwell-centred correlation of block FWHM with acquisition time $r=+0.18$ ($p=0.6$, n=12), and of the position jitter $r=+0.19$ ($p=0.6$) — so sharing is not *refuted* either; it is simply **untested by a design that spread the peaks over an hour**, on 12 points with no power to resolve a slow width wander. So the hierarchical 0.053 stays conditional on an **acquisition-timing assumption the archive can now date but not validate**, which is the real reason it is a cross-check and the conservative model-independent bound is the headline — not merely that it is 'optimistic'. (A fixed-lock session's fix is cheap and already in the plan: interleave the four peaks within minutes, not across an hour.) All fit errors are marginal (full covariance), folding in the $\beta \leftrightarrow \sigma_\text{laser}$ anticorrelation; the estimator spread is the ADDITIONAL model systematic.

> **The lever cross-check (M4d, `run_lever_crosscheck`) — a lever-limited cross-check ESTIMATOR, not the headline $\beta$.** *(Renamed from the misleading `definitive_fit`: it is a cross-check — do not grab `lever_crosscheck.csv` as the headline; that is `beta_self_probe.csv`.)* The model-independent width-slope bound (top row) is the headline; this row is the internally-consistent **70/90/110 °C cooling-sweep** joint fit (one session), whose central value the lever test below shows to be a *bound*, not a measurement. It uses the Lehmann-cusp transit — the **established** Biraben–Cagnac kernel (App. B), so a physics choice, not a coin flip; the Gaussian/Voigt alternative is the deliberate cusp-free *null*, and its $\beta$ spread is the model-form bar. Sharing is per-$T$ $\sigma_\text{laser}$ (M4c-*consistent* — an **in-sample** check, §C2). Its statistical precision and audited systematics per isotope:

| isotope | $\beta$ | statistical | model-form (transit / sharing) | $w_0$-band | drop-a-peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 85Rb | 0.0535 | $\pm$0.0043 | $\pm$0.014 (0.014 / 0.001) | [0.050, 0.057] | 0.0067 (peak 4192) |
| 87Rb | 0.0528 | $\pm$0.0047 | $\pm$0.016 (0.014 / 0.002) | [0.049, 0.057] | 0.0022 (peak 4207) |
> **Read the $\pm0.005$ as this estimator's precision, not $\beta$'s.** It is the cooling-sweep joint-fit covariance — but $\beta$ rides on only **three density points**, so the slope lever is fragile (few effective DOF, heavy-tailed — the same $\sim$factor-2 own-uncertainty the model-independent bound carries), and the **lever test below moves this central value by $\sim8\sigma$**. So 0.053 is a bound wearing an estimator's error budget: treat it as the short-lever end of a lever-dependent range (per-condition $\sim$0.01 → cooling 0.053), and the $\pm0.005$/model-form/$w_0$ bars as the precision and systematics *of this estimator*, which do not span the bound. The headline number stays the top-row width-slope bound.

> Per-drop detail is committed (`beta_loo_drop`/`sigma_loo_drop` rows): dropping the 993.4207 nm suspect moves $\beta_{87}$ by -0.0022 (below its statistical error) and leaves the $\sigma_\text{laser}(T)$ pattern intact (2.05/2.22/1.50 vs 2.05/2.17/1.54 with all peaks) — the suspect drives **neither** the coefficient **nor** the $\sigma_\text{laser}$ trend, whose 110 °C dip M4c already attributes to the $\beta\leftrightarrow\sigma_\text{laser}$ degeneracy. The same holds for every other single-peak drop.


> The **$w_0$-band is the largest systematic** (the OPEN waist — the beam-profile measurement collapses it), then the transit model-form (Lehmann cusp vs Voigt); the $\sigma_\text{laser}$ A-vs-B *sharing* choice is minor — per-block (Model B) gives $\beta_{87}=0.051$ vs per-$T$ 0.053, agreeing to $\sim$0.002, so the per-$T$ headline (the M4c-consistent, physically-motivated choice) is *robust to the sharing choice*. **Drop-a-peak is small** — no single peak, including the 993.4207 nm suspect, drives $\beta$. (Drop-a-*temperature* is large — up to 0.14 if present — but that is expected **lever leverage**: removing one of only three temperatures shortens the density arm; it is a sensitivity diagnostic, not a robustness failure.) A synthetic-injection closure (`tests/test_lever_crosscheck`) confirms the 20-trace machinery recovers a known $\beta$.

> **Lever test — $\beta$ is reported as a bound because $\gamma_\text{coll}$ barely grows with density.** Adding the curated 130 °C anchor (`serves_t130`, 225 mW; density lever $\times16\to\times53$) pulls the joint $\beta$ to [85Rb 0.020; 87Rb 0.022] — well below the cooling-sweep 0.053 and larger than every error bar above. This is **not** one bad block: the per-condition $\gamma_\text{coll}$ rises only $\times$1.5 across the $\times$52 density span (70→130 °C), and the 130 °C widths sit *on* that near-flat trend — whereas a real binary-collision width is **linear** in $N$. So the fitted $\gamma_\text{coll}$ is a residual **floor**, not resolved collisions, and the apparent $\beta$ shrinks as the lever lengthens (per-condition $\beta$ is only $\sim$0.01; the joint 0.053 is $\sigma_\text{laser}$-sharing-inflated). That is precisely why $\beta$ is a BOUND. The 130 °C block is not a separate session — the recovered clock puts it 2.3 h from the 110 °C dwell inside one campaign — but it *is* the extreme end of the lever, so folding it in moves the answer by leverage. A fixed-lock session needs *interleaved* high-density points to resolve any real collisional slope.

*Lifted by:* a fixed lock (removes between-block laser drift) + beam-profile $w_0$ (knife-edge and/or camera; sets the transit subtraction) → a clean measurement.

## C2 — 2025 laser-epoch width $\sigma_\text{laser}$

- **<1.2 MHz (laser axis)** — upper bound over the w0 prior band (60-70um), rising with w0; =0 at w0~16um; conditional on the adopted w0=64um until a beam profile is measured on this bench.
- Degenerate with $w_0$ via transit (M9): the corrected transit adds ~2.1 MHz at $w_0=32$ µm (which OVERSHOOTS the observed line, so 32 µm is excluded) and ~0.93 MHz at the 64 µm prior; more transit leaves less width for the laser.

> **Reconciling the three $\sigma_\text{laser}$ numbers (they are not contradictory — mind the axis).** This C2 bound is $<$1.1 MHz on the **laser** axis; the lever-crosscheck $\sigma_\text{laser}(T)$ (1.48/1.63/1.06) and the Stark-fit core (0.52–0.82) are on the **transition** axis ($=2\times$ laser). Halved, the lever gives laser $\approx$0.53–0.82 and the Stark core $\approx$0.26–0.41 MHz, both under this bound. The 70/90 °C tied values (1.48/1.63 transition) are inflated by the $\beta\leftrightarrow\sigma_\text{laser}$ degeneracy (the free per-condition fit is flatter, $\sim$1.0–1.25 transition); the underlying laser width is $\sim$1.1 transition $=$ ~0.55 laser. Every committed CSV carries the axis in its unit string.

*Lifted by:* beam-profile $w_0$ (knife-edge and/or camera) + a direct linewidth measurement in a fixed-lock session.

## C3 — power sweep (tested against the ramp-law predictions)

- **C3a linewidth — no power trend:** inflation 3–8% across 25–225 mW, non-monotonic (block scatter, not power broadening).
- **C3b amplitude $\propto P^2$:** log-log slopes 1.83–2.12 (two-photon rate law; 993.4121 nm mildly saturates). The power slope is immune to radiation trapping (even at the thick $\tau/$cm$\approx$160): the trapping optical depth is set by the GROUND-state density, which the weak two-photon excitation does not deplete, so the trapping factor is power-independent at fixed T and rescales the amplitude without bending the log-log slope. (This is the operative condition — ground-state non-depletion — not a linear-reabsorption assumption.) This immunity is an ARGUMENT, not tested here: the archival sweep is single-temperature (130 °C, one $\tau$), so slope-vs-$\tau$ cannot be checked — multi-T power sweeps in a fixed-lock session would. 993.4121 nm's low slope (1.83) is unresolved: dim-line SNR bias at 25 mW, genuine saturation, or a weak power-dependence of trapping at the thick end are not separable from one single-T sweep.
- **C3c — the RAMP asymmetry is a bound; the significant low-power skew in `power_sweep.csv` is shot noise, not the ramp.** Two DISTINCT quantities, and conflating them is a trap. (i) The **ramp** skew (the asymmetry coefficient of the fitted ramp$\otimes$core profile, $\propto S_0^3$) is below the SNR floor at $\le$225 mW → an **upper bound**, consistent with zero, as the corrected physics requires (the ramp's first-order shift is absorbed by the per-scan free centre; §THEORY_NOTE 3). (ii) The committed `resid_skew` column is a *different* thing — the residual skewness of a **symmetric**-model fit — and it is large and POSITIVE at low power (up to **~10σ** at 25 mW: 993.4154 nm 0.345±0.036) and **falls** with amplitude as $\sim$amp$^{-0.5}$. That is the Poisson **shot-noise skewness** (the noise is right-skewed $\propto 1/\sqrt{\text{counts}}$, positive, vanishing as the line brightens) — a statistical artifact of the noise, NOT a physical line asymmetry, and the *opposite* power dependence of the ramp ($\propto P^3$ growth). So the 9σ is real but identified: `resid_skew` is a shot-noise-dominated diagnostic, not a ramp signal, and it is why the archival skew cannot serve as a ramp measurement. (Per-peak scaling exponent $-0.2$ to $-0.9$ about the $-0.5$ shot-noise value, so a small extra low-power systematic — baseline, line-pull — is not excluded, but shot noise dominates.) a fixed-lock session would lift the real observable two ways: the fixed lock un-absorbs the large first-order pull, and the small waist ($S_0$ 0.59 → 5.7 MHz, $\approx$10× larger at 225 mW) makes the ramp asymmetry a detection. The naive $S_0^3$ reading (×64) is superseded: the axial average changes the third cumulant's magnitude and, past $Z_c/z_R\approx1.12$, its sign (PLAN §6 #4). Which side of that crossover each configuration sits on is set by $Z_c = L_\parallel/2M$, and that is now largely pinned: the cathode is landscape, so $L_\parallel = 12$ mm and $Z_c = 6/M$ mm, and the PMT is not re-oriented between configurations. The two-waist sign flip then holds for every $M$ from 0.5 to 6 — it no longer waits on measuring the geometry, only its magnitude does ($u$ and $v$ are still unmeasured; $M\approx2.5$–3 by estimate puts the archive at $Z_c\approx2.0$–$2.4$ mm, below the crossover, and config S above it). Conditional also on **two** same-sign small-waist corrections that suppress the skew and must be fit jointly: the §7 beam-divergence axial average (the larger, sign-flipping one) and the standing-wave fringe-resolved tail (~26-28% at 16 µm; THEORY_NOTE §5). See docs/THEORY_NOTE.md §3.

- **C3d — the AC-Stark coefficient, from the power-lever: an UPPER BOUND $S_0$(225 mW) $< 0.64$ MHz (95%, profile likelihood), landing inside the predicted band 0.28–0.40 MHz** (`run_stark_sweep`, M4e — the power-lever twin of the $\beta$ fit). One shared $\kappa$ ($S_0=\kappa P$) is fit to the four peaks' FWHM-vs-power (each floating its core width); the ramp broadens the line as $\sim S_0^2$, the only live handle since the *shift* (pull $\sim S_0$) is dead in the 2025 drift. The fit ($S_0(225) = 0.00$, $\kappa$ consistent with zero) is **not** a measurement; it **brackets** the prediction. The bound and the prediction are independent by construction: the bound uses only the width-vs-power data (no $w_0$ enters), while the prediction is the computed polarizability at the $w_0$ prior, fixed before the fit and never an input to it, so their agreement is a genuine consistency check. That independence is from the density lever and the polarizability, **not** from the lineshape model: like the $\beta$ *fit* (not the model-independent width-slope bound that heads C1), the $\kappa$ fit forward-models each line through `model_profile`, so this bound is conditional on that spectral model. The prediction is not a point but a **band**: the 0.28–0.40 MHz spread is $S_0$ over the $w_0$ prior band 60–70 µm ($\propto 1/w_0^2$; central 0.35 at the adopted 64 µm) folded with $\rho=0.94\pm0.04$, the retro ratio now assumed rather than asserted at 1 ($S_0\propto(1+\rho)$; the in-situ $\rho$ is a fixed-lock-session task, PLAN §3), under the field-intensity convention pinned in THEORY_NOTE §5. **The construction of the 95% is load-bearing and documented:** the best fit rails at $\kappa=0$, where the width handle ($\propto S_0^2$) has zero gradient, so a linearized (Wald) $\kappa+1.645\sigma$ bound has no valid coverage there — its $\sigma$ is a finite-difference artifact (the superseded Wald numbers, 1.0 raw / 2.4 inflated MHz, stay in the CSV as diagnostics). The quoted bound is instead a **profile-likelihood** limit: $\kappa$ is scanned upward with the per-peak cores re-minimized at each point, and the limit sits where $\chi^2$ rises by $2.706\times\chi^2_\text{red}$ — the threshold scaling that carries the over-dispersion ($\chi^2_\text{red}\approx5$, block-to-block width scatter) into the bound, conservatively — though as one global factor: it treats the over-dispersion as homogeneous across the width points, while the scatter is block-level (a block bootstrap of the profile limit would be the sharper construction; not run on the archive). The result says the bound falls inside the prediction band, excluding the tight-waist (high-$S_0$) top of it while the lower reach and zero remain allowed. Read that as a bracket, not a sensitivity claim: the predicted effect at 225 mW is ~0.09 MHz against a single-block width scatter of 0.088 MHz, so the bound is produced entirely by averaging over blocks — and M17 finds that averaging assumption untested (permutation p = 0.11, neither established nor excluded). *Lifted by:* a fixed lock would measure the pull $\sim S_0$ directly, and the small waist would make $S_0$ several-fold larger — turning this bound into the coefficient.

- **C3e — the CENTRE channel cannot measure the pull, and the failure is unidentifiability rather than imprecision** (`run_stark_centres`, M21). The AC-Stark shift moves the line centre as $\propto S_0$, which is a stronger dependence than the width's $\propto S_0^2$, so the centres ought to be the better channel. They are not, for a reason that is a design fault and not a statistical shortfall. Peak positions are only frequencies within a *display epoch* (a run of unchanged scope horizontal position — see `run_laser_history`'s retraction), so each epoch carries a free offset; of the 26 epochs covering the power sweep only **three** contrast two powers at all, each a 50 mW step, and no epoch spans two lines. Inside those three, power still descends with time, exactly as the campaign was run. Fitting a shared pull against three drift forms therefore gives $|S_0(225\ \mathrm{mW})| < 9.49$, $< 14.57$ and $< 17.65$ MHz for linear, one-exponential and two-exponential drift — and the pull's **sign flips** between the first two (+3.4 vs -3.3 MHz/W) while the bound degrades monotonically as the drift model gains freedom. A merely imprecise parameter does neither. The best of the three is 15× weaker than C3d's width bound, so the width channel carries the light-shift information and the centres carry none. Tagged NULL, not BOUND. **The design consequence is the deliverable:** cycle or randomise the power ordering so drift is orthogonal to the pull, *and* leave the horizontal position alone — or log it — because every move severs the centre record. A superseded $< 7.3$ MHz version of this bound was tighter only because it differenced positions across those moves. **A second, stronger attempt failed on the signal's own shape.** Referencing each centre to its own display window (the peak position minus the window start) is exactly knob-immune and collapses the campaign scatter from 7.75 to 0.28 MHz; fitting a pull on it returns $S_0(225) = +0.89\pm0.27$ MHz, apparently $3.3\sigma$. It is not one. An AC-Stark pull is **linear in $P$ by construction**, and free per-rung offsets reject linearity at $F(3,91) = 4.49$, $p = 0.0055$: the rung means are non-monotone (+0.243 MHz at 25 mW against $-$0.137 at 225 mW, so the highest power sits above the middle ones). Dropping the 25 mW rung leaves $+0.10\pm0.22$ MHz over a threefold power range. That rung is also the worst to lean on: SNR 18 against 193, scatter 4.6$\times$ larger, and the only level where the sweep retrace makes a second above-half-max region (8 of 20 traces, against 0 of 79). The apparent significance is inflated besides -- the 99 traces are 20 conditions of ~5 repeats, intraclass correlation 0.38, and a block bootstrap gives $[-0.31, +1.86]$. Not the estimator's fault: five independent centre estimators agree to $\pm$0.02 MHz.

- **C3f — the joint three-session fit puts the light-shift bound to $S_0(225\ \mathrm{mW}) < 0.15$ MHz** (`run_stark_joint`, M23; 95% one-sided profile likelihood). Instead of C3d's 20 summary widths, every point of every canonical power-sweep profile enters a joint maximum-likelihood fit — 100/46/26 traces across three sessions — with one shared $\kappa$ ($S_0=\kappa P$), per-peak physical widths under a $\gamma_\mathrm{coll}$ prior from the archive's own $\beta_\mathrm{self}\times N(130°C)$ chain, per-trace free centres (drift and re-locks are profiled out exactly, not modelled), and a per-session detector-saturation nuisance that fits linear — the instrument's receipt. The second session is the 2025-07-04 LeCroy dress rehearsal (46 usable traces; 90/180/270 mW), whose 270 mW rung carries 1.44× the campaign's maximum $S_0^2$ lever and whose alternating ladder directions are the design M21 demanded — though its auto-triggered scope randomises the sweep phase per trace, so it contributes shape and width, not centres. The third session is the campaign-morning pilot: 26 traces on one peak at 35–210 mW and the campaign's cell temperature, on the campaign instrument twenty minutes after the ruler's commissioning, its axis riding the campaign bracket rate through a ±10% nuisance licensed by the raw width ratio (0.971 at matched conditions). Its centres also stay out: the recorded window starts step with the power changes in the pull's own direction, M21's response-versus-relabel ambiguity in miniature. The profile minimum sits at $\kappa = 0.00$ MHz/W, only $\Delta\chi^2 = 0.0$ below $\kappa=0$ — consistent with no shift at all (mid-run readings of the FORWARD chain alone suggested a detection near the predicted $\kappa$; the backward pass polished $\kappa=0$ down and the preference vanished, which is why only bidirectional profiles are quoted here). **The bound sits below the prediction, and that is the result.** Against $S_0(225) = 0.35$ MHz predicted at the adopted $w_0=64$ µm with $\rho=0.94$, the fit gives 2.3× less. The spread across data subsets is the dominant systematic — 0.15 MHz from all three sessions, 0.22 from the campaign rows alone, and 0.35 with peak 4192 dropped (which removes the entire pilot). The retro ratio cannot absorb that: $S_0\propto(1+\rho)$ buys at most a factor 2 even at $\rho=0$. The intensity must be lower than the prior assumes, and the most conservative subset already requires a lower intensity than even the adopted prior assumes. That prior is itself now the lineage measurement — [Rajasree 2020](lit/rajasree2020thesis.md) recorded 128 µm diameter on the same laser model, lens and geometry — so the comparison is no longer an inference pointing at an external number but a direct test of it, and the bound still lands under it. Further robustness: dropping any one peak leaves the predicted $\kappa$ rejection intact (LOPO rows); and the rehearsal axis-direction hypothesis check did not converge in this run (a cold start on the flipped rehearsal axis; the converged wing-variant pair of the same directions agrees to a few tens of $\chi^2$, and a seeded re-run is in progress). One piece of residual structure survived this fit: a same-physical-side near-core asymmetry in both sessions, absorbed by neither a detector time constant (killed at $+2200$ for 10 ms) nor the wing nuisance. C3g closes it.

- **C3g — the residual asymmetry is not a collisional wing; C3f's open item is closed** (`run_wing_check`, M24). A quasistatic self-broadening satellite is a pair effect, so its fractional weight must scale with density, and the temperature sweep holds a ×52 density lever at fixed 225 mW while the Stark wedge and any instrument asymmetry stay put. The observable is the **difference** between the two sides, red minus blue: a symmetric mismatch between the fixed transit kernel and the free core raises both wings together and is not an asymmetry, so only the difference answers the question. It returns **-0.0007 ± 0.0013** of peak at 130 °C, 0.5σ, exactly where a collisional satellite would be 52× enhanced, and no temperature exceeds 0.7σ. The power lever agrees: at fixed density the fitted fraction does not hold constant as a physical wing must, but tracks amplitude, exactly as C3c's shot-noise identification of the residual skew already said. Both levers contradict a physical wing, so the asymmetry M23 flagged is amplitude-linked statistics, nothing about it enters the Stark budget, and the satellite thread is closed on this archive. A real satellite search needs the fixed-lock session's SNR at 150–170 °C, where this same estimator would resolve a 0.001-fraction wing at many sigma.


> **The sensitivity behind the null (M13).** A bound is only interpretable next to the effect size the analysis could actually have caught, so the same injection-recovery machinery is run forward: the **minimum detectable effect** is $\beta \approx$ **0.05** at 50% and **0.14** at 95% detection probability (MHz per 10¹² cm⁻³). The archive was therefore genuinely sensitive at the 0.05–0.14 level and saw nothing — the null is a real constraint, not an insensitive experiment — while the quoted headline bound sits *above* that, deliberately, through the t(0.95,1) and density-scale inflations (C1). At $\beta=0$ the SNR rule alone fires 6% of the time, close to its nominal 5%, which is the calibration check on the detection rule itself.

## Sensitivity at a glance

The referee question — *what moves if an assumption moves* — in one table, generated live from `lever_crosscheck.csv` and `stark_sweep.csv` so it cannot go stale (β_self entries in MHz per 10¹² cm⁻³; full prose reading in C1/C3d above).

| vary this | β_self moves by (85Rb · 87Rb) | reading |
|---|---|---|
| the OPEN w₀ (transit band, ~65→40 µm) | spans 0.050–0.057 · 0.049–0.057 | the dominant systematic — a beam-profile measurement collapses it |
| transit model-form (Lehmann cusp ↔ Voigt) | 0.014 · 0.016 | comparable to β_self itself — part of why the headline is a bound |
| σ_laser sharing (per-T ↔ per-block) | 0.001 · 0.002 | negligible next to the other two rows |
| the M1 noise law (measured σ(V) ↔ uniform weights) | ≤ 0.003 · ≤ 0.018 | the weights are not doing physics — the largest shift is on the 993.4207 nm suspect peak |
| drop any one peak | ≤ 0.007 · ≤ 0.002 | no single line drives the result |
| drop one temperature | up to 0.14 · 0.07 | lever leverage with three densities — expected, not fragility |
| add the ×53 130 °C lever | -0.034 · -0.031 | pulls β_self down — the width is a floor, not resolved collisions (C1) |

| vary this | the S₀(225 mW) bound | reading |
|---|---|---|
| the OPEN w₀ | unchanged | the bound uses width-vs-power only; only the *prediction* is w₀- and ρ-conditional |
| bound construction (Wald ↔ profile) | 1.0 / 2.4 → 0.64 MHz | Wald has no coverage at the κ = 0 rail; the profile limit is the quoted bound |
| per-peak core widths | absorbed | each peak's core floats per power — laser-epoch drift cannot fake a κ |

## Supporting results

- **Frequency axis (M2):** 0.04253(5) MHz/ms laser axis. The 20 ruler blocks disagree by more than their own statistical errors ($\chi^2_\text{red}=8.1$), and the quoted error is PDG-inflated by $\sqrt{\chi^2_\text{red}}\approx2.8\times$ to cover it. The scatter is block level: before/after brackets drift within a session rather than the peaks moving in step, so it widens the common axis error without biasing a cross-peak comparison such as $\beta_{85}$ vs $\beta_{87}$. Each science block uses its own condition's rate, and the sweep is linear across the window to $<0.3$%. The single largest outlier is 993.4207 nm after at +1.5% from the campaign mean. Dropping it moves the campaign rate by -0.07% (0.6$\sigma$) and $\chi^2_\text{red}$ from 8.1 to 5.0: the inflation already covers it, so it stays in by the pre-registered policy of reviewing outliers rather than cutting them.
- **σ_laser sharing (M4c) — an IN-SAMPLE consistency check, not a proof:** at 70/90/110 °C the four peak-blocks agree on one σ_laser (χ²/dof 0.28/0.59/0.29, all $<$1), consistent with the per-T sharing the global fit assumes. Two limits: (i) agreement is **necessary, not sufficient** — the four peaks could have co-drifted between acquisitions and still agree; only logged timestamps (a fixed-lock session) settle it. (ii) It is **in-sample**: the check uses 70/90/110 °C and the headline fit uses the *same* three temperatures, so it cannot be an out-of-sample test — the 130 °C block that would stress the assumption is excluded from it (§C1 lever test). (iii) **The test is under-powered:** χ²/dof of 0.28/0.59/0.29 are *well below 1*, so the peaks agree only within error bars that are themselves $\sim$1.2–2.2× too large (the conservative $\tau_\text{int}$ noise inflation over-estimates them). At these χ² the data cannot discriminate shared from unshared — so the sharing is **untested**, not merely unverifiable. So it answers the acquisition-timing worry as *consistency*, not confirmation. But the *free* per-condition σ_laser is $\sim$flat (1.5–1.7), while the β·N-tied global fit inflates it to 1.5–2.2 across the sweep: that σ_laser(T) trend is the **β↔σ_laser degeneracy** under the density constraint, NOT a physical laser drift — so the trend is a model artifact, not a stale block, and it does not corrupt β (the density lever still pins the collisional slope). Reproducible: `run_sigma_laser_sharing.py`.
- **Lehmann cusp (M8):** ΔBIC(Voigt−Lehmann) -0.1…+3.7 — no preference for the cusp (the negative end is a mild dispreference on 993.4207 nm), all far below the gate ≥10; needs the fixed-lock session's narrow laser.
- **Radiation trapping (M7):** amplitude ∝ N, log-log slopes 0.85–1.02 (no significant rollover), though the cell is optically THICK on D1 (τ/cm≈1–160) — trapping redistributes rather than destroys the collected 795 nm signal. Degeneracy-breaking (peak-differential) trapping is sought and NOT found: ⁸⁵Rb is nominally 0.09±0.08 more sublinear than ⁸⁷Rb (right sign, ~1σ); the 30–50% ratio disagreement (M10) is NON-monotonic in density ⇒ drift, not trapping.
- **Degeneracy law (M10):** areas should be abundance×(2F+1) (5/3, 7/5 within-isotope); measured ratios swing 30–50% between blocks (drift) — not testable in the archive; a fixed-lock session: interleave peaks.
- **Dynamic polarizabilities (M16):** an independent sum-over-states recompute of $\Delta\alpha(993)=\alpha_{6S}-\alpha_{5S}$ gives **-1145 a.u.** — $|\Delta\alpha|$ within $\sim$5% of Orson et al.'s 1093, but the **opposite sign** (a blue transition shift); the sign is an open theory item flagged for external adjudication (THEORY_NOTE §5), and every archival result is sign-immune ($S_0$ bounds and the asymmetry null use $|\Delta\alpha|$). Validation against anchors the model does not use: the measured 5S tune-out 790.032326(32) nm (Leonard 2015 as corrected by their 2017 erratum, PRA 95 059901(E), both now held; the superseded 2015 value was 790.032388(32), 0.062 pm away) is reproduced at 790.0339 nm ($\approx$1.6 pm), the measured static $\alpha_{5S}$ 318.79(1.42) at 318.28, and the static $\alpha_{6S}$ tail is calibrated to Safronova's 5167(22) (5167). The same model gives the **first 5S–6S magic wavelengths** (scalar, ENVELOPE): $\lambda_m \approx$ 1203.9 / 1287.9 / 1339.6 nm — a trap at any of them would hold both states without pulling the 993 nm line. Scalar only — which is exact for these $J=1/2$ states under linear polarization, the tensor term vanishing by the triangle rule; the vector term matters only for circular components near the 6S–5P lines. Nearest prior work in the same band is Zang *et al.* 2012 (arXiv:1204.4354), which reports six magic wavelengths between 1200 and 1600 nm for the **6s–5p** pairs of a four-level active clock: 1342 and 1421 nm for 6s–5p_1/2, and 1331, 1336, 1453, 1461 nm for 6s–5p_3/2. Two of them bracket the 1339.6 here (1336 and 1342), which is expected rather than suspicious: every 6S-involving root in this band is confined between the 5p_1/2–6s_1/2 and 5p_3/2–6s_1/2 resonances at 1323.88 and 1366.87 nm, a 43 nm window. Different state pair and different magic condition, so the claim is specifically 5S–6S. A trapped-atom platform is the follow-up. Reproducible: `run_polarizability.py`.

### M17 — resolving power: why each result has the status it has (DIAGNOSTIC)

An observable can only answer a question if it moves more across the conditions than it scatters when nothing physical changes. Both are measurable: the dynamic range over the 70–130 °C sweep, and the block-to-block scatter at fixed conditions taken from the 130 °C power ladder, where width is power-independent. Their ratio:

| observable | dynamic range in block-noise units | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `amplitude` | 45.1 | resolves |
| `total_fwhm` | 6.0 | marginal |
| `gamma_coll` | 2.7 | cannot resolve |
| `sigma_laser` | 2.5 | cannot resolve |

The ratio reproduces this ledger's own status assignments, each of which was argued separately and by different means: amplitude clears the floor 45× and is the one place the archive extracts a number (the cold spot, ΔT ≈ +20 K); the widths sit at 2.5–6.0 and are exactly where it reports bounds.

It is also predictive, which is the point. PLAN §3 asks for two things — hot points at 150–170 °C to grow the signal, and interleaving with per-trace power logging to cut the block noise. Hot points alone reach only 0.9–3.0σ per block; with the noise cut 4× as well, 3.4–12.2σ. **Both halves of the prescription are load-bearing** — the second is not a refinement of the first. Reproducible: `run_resolving_power.py`.

The same lens on the *power* axis finds an untested assumption. The S₀ bound (M4e) inflates its errors by $\sqrt{\chi^2}$ to absorb block scatter, which is the right remedy only if that scatter averages down — and the predicted ramp broadening at 225 mW is almost exactly one single-block scatter, so the bound rests on it. A permutation test against the independence null returns p = 0.21: neither established nor excluded, because four peaks by five powers cannot resolve it. Untested rather than wrong; `PLAN.md` §7 now asks for the returned-to block that would settle it.
